In November 2025, a devastating house fire destroyed Ruth Mary Repuyan and her family’s home in Ilocos Sur, Philippines. Returning on November 27, they found nearly everything reduced to black ash and melted debris.

While searching through the rubble, Repuyan discovered their family Bible almost completely untouched by the flames. In a video, she gently flips through its pages, which remain intact and unmarked, while a nearby book was heavily damaged.

“We will celebrate Christmas with nothing left,” Repuyan said. “Everything was burnt, and the only thing we have is the Bible. This is a miracle.”

The discovery has brought comfort and hope to the family amid their loss. Many people who saw the video were moved by this powerful moment of resilience and faith. The story continues to inspire others facing difficult times, reminding them that hope can be found even in the most challenging situations.

(Photo: Ruth Mary Repuyan)

LOOK: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. inspects the G. Araneta Drainage Improvement Project along E. Rodriguez Sr. Avenue in Quezon City. 

The project involves installing two 1.50-meter-diameter High-Density Polyethylene  pipes as part of the upgrading and rehabilitation of the existing drainage system. 

It aims to address recurring flooding along G. Araneta Avenue, from Kaliraya Street to E. Rodriguez Sr. Avenue, with the drainage ultimately discharging into the San Juan River. | @luisacabatoINQ
